geo_ui_get_state_tool.name: geo_ui_get_state_tool
geo_ui_get_state_tool.description:
Read the current application state as a GeoIntent.

Use this to observe what is on screen — typically when continuing an
iterative analysis: read current state, decide what to change, emit a
new GeoIntent via geo_ui_render_intent_tool. The user may have changed
the view by hand since your last render.

OUTPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **intent**: GeoIntent describing the application state.

viewport.description:
Spatial viewport.

`bbox` is interpreted in `crs`. For the geographic default
(`EPSG:4326`), `bbox` is `[west, south, east, north]` in degrees.
For projected CRSs, the values are projected coordinates.
`bbox=None` means "app default extent."

anyOf.description:
Time selection.

Either a single `instant` OR a closed range `{start, end}` — the two
are mutually exclusive. All fields `None` is allowed and means
"app default time."

items.description:
A reference to a renderable layer.

`id` is application-defined — the conforming app must be able to
resolve it to a layer in its own catalogue. Per-layer rendering hints
beyond the universal set (`visible`, `opacity`) belong in extensions
and are expressed as namespaced extra keys
(e.g. `"raster-styling:palettes": [...]`).

geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool.name: geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool
geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool.description:
List the intent extensions and the layers this application supports.

Call this first in a conversation. Each extension entry names it
(compare, raster-styling, ...), says where its fields live (`scope`:
"intent" = namespaced keys on the GeoIntent root, "layer" = namespaced
keys on each LayerRef), gives a one-line summary of when to use it, its
namespaced `keys`, which of them are `required`, and the JSON schema of
its fields. `layers` lists the layer ids the application can show, with
titles and temporal coverage; a GeoIntent may only reference those ids.

Decide which extensions the user's request needs, then fill only their
namespaced fields in the GeoIntent you pass to geo_ui_render_intent_tool.
Supported extensions are pre-declared by that tool, so never write
`geoui_extensions` yourself; fields of an unsupported extension and
unknown layer ids are rejected.

OUTPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **extensions**: The supported intent extensions, in the order the application lists them.
- **layers**: The layers the application can show; GeoIntent layer ids must come from here.

extensions.description: The supported intent extensions, in the order the application lists them.

items.description: One supported extension, as ``ExtensionSpec.describe()`` lays it out.

scope.description: "intent": keys on the GeoIntent root; "layer": keys on each LayerRef.

summary.description: When to use it, in one line.

required.description: Keys that must be present once the extension is used.

fields_schema.description: JSON schema of the fields (without the prefix).

layers.description: The layers the application can show; GeoIntent layer ids must come from here.

items.description: One layer the application can show; ``id`` is what a GeoIntent's ``layers[].id`` must use.

id.description: Layer id as the application resolves it.

end.description: Last available date, or null when ongoing.

period.description: ISO 8601 duration between steps, e.g. P1D.

time.description: Temporal coverage, when the layer is time-varying.

geo_ui_render_intent_tool.name: geo_ui_render_intent_tool
geo_ui_render_intent_tool.description:
Render a GeoIntent in the open map application.

Use this tool to materialise the agent's intended application state
(expressed as a GeoIntent) on screen. The agent reasons in GeoIntent
terms, not in the application's own controls. Rendering REPLACES the
whole state: fields you leave out return to the application's defaults
(compare off, styling cleared, default time and extent), so read the
state first and resend what must stay. Returns the state the
application settled on.

INPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **intent**: GeoIntent describing the desired application state. Core fields: viewport (bbox [west, south, east, north] in degrees, crs EPSG:4326), time (instant, ISO date), layers (id + visible + opacity). Extensions and the layer catalogue come from the application: call geo_ui_list_intent_extensions_tool first. Supported extensions are pre-declared by this tool: do not write `geoui_extensions`; just add the namespaced fields the request needs. Fields of an unsupported extension and unknown layer ids are rejected. Rendering replaces the whole state.

OUTPUT FIELD DESCRIPTIONS:
- **intent**: GeoIntent describing the application state.
- **settled**: True when the application confirmed the state was applied on screen; false when it timed out waiting.

intent.description:
The GeoUI Protocol root.

Carries the minimal cross-application contract: viewport, time,
layers. Extension fields are namespaced (e.g. `"compare:layers"`)
and live as extra keys; their semantics are defined by the schemas
pointed to by `geoui_extensions`.

Either a single `instant` OR a closed range `{start, end}` — the two
